title: Linkability of sensor telemetry to user identity
description: Continuous collection of GPS position, heart rate, step counts, and timestamps enables linking of data points to reconstruct user movement patterns, daily routines, and health behaviors, potentially revealing sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Device stores or transmits data with sufficient granularity to enable pattern analysis

title: Identifiability through biometric and location data
description: The combination of GPS coordinates, timestamps, and biometric data (heart rate) creates a unique data fingerprint that could identify the specific user, especially when cross-referenced with other data sources.
assumptions: Data is stored or transmitted in a form that preserves identifying characteristics

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensor data
description: Sensor telemetry data transmitted from user to wearable device could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or storage.
assumptions: Data transmission or storage lacks adequate encryption or access controls

title: Data aggregation revealing sensitive patterns
description: Continuous aggregation of multiple data types (heart rate, steps, GPS, timestamps) enables inference of sensitive information beyond individual data points, such as health conditions, lifestyle habits, or location preferences.
assumptions: Multiple data streams are combined and analyzed over time

title: User unawareness of data collection scope
description: Users may not be fully aware of the extent of data being collected, how long it is retained, who has access to it, or how it may be used for secondary purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices are unclear or users do not read them carefully

title: Device ID enables user identification
description: The wearable device transmits its unique device ID along with sensor data, which can be used to identify and track the specific user across sessions and potentially link to other data sources.
assumptions: Device ID is unique and persistent per device/user

title: GPS traces disclose sensitive location information
description: GPS traces transmitted from the wearable device reveal precise location data, including home, workplace, and movement patterns, which constitutes sensitive personal information.
assumptions: GPS data is transmitted in sufficient detail to reconstruct movement patterns

title: Potential over-collection of sensor data
description: The wearable device may transmit more sensor data than strictly necessary for the companion app's functionality, violating the data minimality principle. Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps may include data beyond what is required.
assumptions: Not all transmitted sensor data is strictly necessary for app functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific app requirements and data processing purposes

title: User unawareness of data transmission scope
description: Users may not be fully aware of what sensor data (GPS, exercise metrics, timestamps) is being transmitted from the wearable device to the companion app, or how frequently this occurs.
assumptions: User consent/awareness mechanisms may not clearly communicate data transmission details

title: Linkability of activity data across sessions
description: Exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps can be linked across multiple sync events to build comprehensive profiles of user behavior, routines, and locations over time.
assumptions: Data from multiple sync sessions can be correlated and aggregated

title: User unawareness of health data collection scope
description: The user may not be fully aware of what health data (calorie intake, meals, weight) is being collected, how it will be used, stored, or shared with third parties when manually logging entries in the companion app.
assumptions: User has limited understanding of app's data practices and privacy policy

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health data
description: The health data entered by the user (calorie intake, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through app vulnerabilities, data breaches, or improper access controls in the companion app.
assumptions: App stores or transmits health data that could be exposed

title: Data aggregation revealing detailed health patterns
description: Individual entries of calorie intake, meals, and weight could be aggregated over time to reveal detailed patterns about the user's health status, eating habits, lifestyle, and potentially sensitive health conditions.
assumptions: App retains historical data and performs aggregation or analysis

title: Linkability of health data to user identity
description: The health data entered in the app can be linked to the specific user's identity, creating a comprehensive health profile that could be used for profiling, discrimination, or other purposes beyond the user's intent.
assumptions: App maintains user accounts and links data to identifiable user profiles

title: Excessive Health Data Collection
description: The companion app may collect and store more health data than necessary (calorie intake, weight history, exercise sessions) without clear justification for each data element, violating the data minimality principle.
assumptions: App collects all health metrics without granular user control or purpose limitation

title: Unauthorized Access to Health Log Store
description: The health log store containing sensitive personal health data (weight, exercise, calorie intake) could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls or security vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Data store has authentication/authorization mechanisms that could be bypassed

title: User Unawareness of Data Storage
description: Users may not be fully aware that their health logs are being stored persistently, what specific data elements are retained, or how long the data is kept in the health log store.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain data storage practices

title: Health Data Regulatory Non-Compliance
description: Storage of health-related personal data may not comply with applicable regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) regarding data protection, retention periods, or user rights for health information.
assumptions: Health data is subject to specific regulatory requirements
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and specific health data classification

title: Linkability of Health Data to User Identity
description: Health log data written to the store could be linked to specific user identities, potentially enabling profiling or correlation with other personal data sources.
assumptions: Health logs contain or can be associated with user identifiers

title: Excessive Location Data Collection
description: The app writes GPS location traces with timestamps to the location history store. This may collect more location data than strictly necessary for the app's functionality, violating the minimality principle. Continuous location tracking could be considered implicit disclosure beyond what users reasonably expect.
assumptions: Location tracking is continuous or more frequent than required for core app functionality

title: User Unawareness of Location Tracking
description: Users may not be fully aware that their GPS location traces with timestamps are being continuously written to a persistent data store. The scope and duration of location data collection may not be clearly communicated.
assumptions: Privacy notices do not clearly explain the extent of location data collection and storage

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The location history store containing GPS traces with timestamps could be accessed by unauthorized parties through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or insider threats. Location data is highly sensitive personal information.
assumptions: Data store has appropriate access controls and encryption

title: Location Data Enables User Identification
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be used to identify individuals, especially when combined with other data sources. Location patterns are often unique to individuals and can reveal sensitive information about their habits and routines.
assumptions: Location data is stored with user identifiers or can be linked to user accounts

title: Linkability of Location Data Across Contexts
description: Location history data could be linked with other data about the same individual across different contexts or time periods, creating comprehensive profiles of user behavior and movements.
assumptions: Location data can be correlated with other user data in the system

title: Cross-session health data linkability
description: The Health Analytics Service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across multiple sessions, enabling the creation of comprehensive health profiles by linking data points that were previously isolated. This aggregation allows correlation of health behaviors over time, potentially revealing sensitive patterns about an individual's health condition, lifestyle, and medical status.
assumptions: The analytics service has access to session identifiers or timestamps that enable linking records across different time periods.

title: Excessive health data collection for analytics
description: The analytics service may be collecting more health data than strictly necessary for health-condition analysis. Reading all calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions could violate the data minimality principle if not all data points are required for the stated analytical purpose.
assumptions: The health-condition analysis does not require all historical health log data, or could be performed with aggregated/anonymized data instead of raw individual records.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain whether the analytics truly requires all raw data or if data minimization has been properly assessed.

title: User unawareness of cross-session health analysis
description: Users may not be aware that their health logs are being read and analyzed across multiple sessions for health-condition analysis. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent and awareness of how their personal health data is being processed.
assumptions: Privacy notices or consent mechanisms do not clearly communicate the cross-session analytics capability to users.

title: Health log identifiability through data patterns
description: Health logs containing calorie, weight, and exercise data may contain patterns that could identify individuals, especially when combined across sessions. Even without direct identifiers, the unique combination of health metrics and temporal patterns could enable re-identification.
assumptions: The health logs contain sufficient granularity and temporal detail to create unique health signatures for individuals.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the level of detail in the health logs and whether direct identifiers are present.

title: Cross-session location data linking
description: The Health Analytics Service queries location history across multiple sessions to derive daily routines and movement patterns, enabling linkage of separate data points to create comprehensive behavioral profiles of individuals.
assumptions: Location history contains sufficient granularity to enable meaningful pattern analysis across time periods

title: Movement pattern identifiability
description: Daily routine and movement patterns derived from location history can serve as unique behavioral identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individuals even if direct identifiers are removed.
assumptions: Movement patterns are sufficiently unique to individuals to enable identification

title: Implicit data disclosure through pattern analysis
description: Deriving daily routines and movement patterns from location history constitutes implicit disclosure of sensitive behavioral information that may not be explicitly consented to by users.
assumptions: Users may not fully understand that location data will be analyzed to derive behavioral patterns

title: Unawareness of cross-session analysis
description: Users may be unaware that their location history is being analyzed across multiple sessions to derive movement patterns and daily routines, rather than just being stored for individual session purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate cross-session analytics capabilities

title: Health condition inference disclosure
description: The analytics service transmits inferred health-condition risk indicators and trend flags to the mobile app. If this data is intercepted or accessed without authorization, it reveals sensitive health information that can identify the data subject's medical status and conditions.
assumptions: The flow contains personally identifiable health inferences that could be used to identify or profile the data subject's health status.

title: Unauthorized access to health analytics data
description: Inferred health insights (risk indicators, routine summaries, trend flags) transmitted from the analytics service to the mobile app could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through insecure transmission channels or improper access controls.
assumptions: The data flow may not have adequate encryption or access controls to prevent unauthorized interception or access.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data
description: The transmission of sensitive health inferences may not be accompanied by adequate cybersecurity risk management practices, potentially violating healthcare data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) that require specific safeguards for health-related personal data.
assumptions: Health analytics data requires special regulatory compliance measures that may not be fully implemented in the data flow security controls.
uncertainty_note: Context Nc.3 retrieved but specific regulatory framework not confirmed for this system.

title: User unawareness of health inference processing
description: Users of the companion mobile app may not be aware that the analytics service is generating and transmitting inferred health insights (risk indicators, trend flags) about their health status, limiting their ability to make informed decisions about data processing.
assumptions: The app may not provide clear transparency about what health inferences are being generated and transmitted to the user.

title: Unauthorized access to health risk indicators
description: The app dashboard displays sensitive health inferences (eating disorder or diabetes risk signals) to the user. If the mobile app lacks proper authentication, encryption, or session management, unauthorized parties could access this sensitive health information through device compromise, shoulder surfing, or network interception.
assumptions: Mobile device security controls may be insufficient; app may not implement proper access controls

title: User unawareness of inference methodology and implications
description: Users may not fully understand how eating disorder or diabetes risk indicators are calculated, what data sources inform these inferences, or the potential consequences of receiving such health-related information. This lack of awareness could lead to inappropriate health decisions or anxiety.
assumptions: App may not provide clear explanations of inference algorithms or data sources

title: Non-compliance with health data regulations
description: Displaying inferred health conditions (eating disorder or diabetes risk) may violate healthcare regulations (HIPAA, GDPR, etc.) regarding medical advice, informed consent, data accuracy requirements, and appropriate disclosure of health-related information to users.
assumptions: App may not have proper legal review for health-related inferences; consent mechanisms may be inadequate
uncertainty_note: Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and whether app is classified as medical device

title: Full health and location dataset transferred to third-party cloud provider
description: The flow transfers the complete health and location dataset to an external cloud hosting provider. This represents a data disclosure across a system boundary. The minimality principle may be violated if all this data is not strictly required for the cloud provider's hosting function.
assumptions: The cloud provider is a third-party external entity outside the organization's direct control

title: Identifiability risk from health and location data transfer
description: Health and location data transferred to the cloud provider may contain or enable identification of individuals, especially if combined with other data the provider may have access to.
assumptions: The health and location dataset contains or can be linked to personally identifiable information

title: Individuals unaware of data transfer to third-party cloud provider
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their health and location data is being transferred to and stored at an external cloud hosting provider, limiting their ability to exercise privacy rights.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose third-party cloud hosting arrangements

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance for health data transfer
description: Transferring health data to a third-party cloud provider may violate healthcare data protection regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) if proper safeguards, contracts, or jurisdictional requirements are not met.
assumptions: Health data is subject to specific regulatory requirements that may restrict third-party transfers
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific jurisdiction and regulatory framework applicable to this system
